bin_override.help: Override the auto-detected llama-server executable — point this at a custom build (e.g. a different backend, or a newer version), or paste a direct download URL to a release archive (.zip/.tar.gz) to fetch and install it automatically. Leave blank to use the bundled/auto-detected one.
bin_override.hint: Local binary path or a download URL...
bin_override.label: llama-server binary:
ctx_size.help: Maximum number of tokens (roughly, word-pieces) of conversation llama.cpp keeps in memory at once — prompt plus reply combined. Bigger means it remembers more of a long chat/document, but uses more RAM/VRAM and can respond slower. Typical values: 2048-4096 for short chats, 8192-16384 for longer ones, 32768+ only for large documents on machines with memory to spare.
ctx_size.label: Context size:
extra_args.help:
Appended verbatim to the llama-server command, after the built-in options (port/context size/GPU layers). Space-separated; wrap a value containing spaces in "double quotes". An invalid or unsupported flag will make the server fail to start — check the log pane at the bottom of the main window if Start doesn't work.

Examples:
--threads 8         number of CPU threads to use
--flash-attn on     enable flash attention (faster; needs support)
--batch-size 512    tokens processed per batch
--no-mmap           disable memory-mapping the model file
--rope-freq-base 0  override RoPE frequency base (long-context models)
extra_args.label: Extra command-line arguments:
models_dir.help: Where models fetched via the "Model" box (download/import/search) or "Look up online" are saved and read back from. The models bundled with the app itself live in their own read-only folder regardless of this.
models_dir.label: Downloaded models folder:
n_gpu_layers.help: How many of the model's layers to run on the GPU instead of the CPU. 999 (default) offloads every layer llama.cpp can — fastest, if the model fits in your GPU's VRAM. 0 = CPU only. If Start crashes or the log shows an out-of-memory error, the model likely doesn't fit in VRAM — try a smaller number (e.g. 20-40) to offload only part of it, or 0 to fall back to CPU entirely.
n_gpu_layers.label: GPU layers:
port.help: TCP port llama-server listens on, on this machine only (127.0.0.1) — never exposed to your network. The default 8080 is fine unless something else on your system is already using it; any free port from 1-65535 works.
port.label: Port:
runtime.apply_path_help: Point at an already-downloaded llama-server executable on disk, or leave blank to reset to the bundled/auto-detected one.
runtime.apply_url_help: Download and install a llama-server build from this direct URL (e.g. a release asset link copied from GitHub), then switch to it automatically — no need to go through "Look up llama.cpp builds" first.
runtime.confirm_body: Delete the installed build "{label}" from disk? This can't be undone.
runtime.filter_help: Narrow the list below by tag, filename, or backend (CUDA/Vulkan/SYCL/ROCm/CPU) — matched against what's already listed, no extra lookup.
runtime.installed_help: llama-server builds downloaded via "Look up llama.cpp builds" in an earlier run, most recently installed first — still listed here even once that list (which only ever shows a handful of the most recent GitHub releases) no longer includes them. "Use" switches to one instantly, with no re-download.
runtime.lookup_help: List recent llama-server builds published on llama.cpp's own GitHub releases, filtered to ones that match this machine's OS/CPU. Picking one downloads and installs it under ~/.quickai/llama-bin and applies it automatically — useful when the current binary can't load a model (e.g. a newer architecture) or doesn't match your GPU.
